stem: What is the primary clinical distinction between localized bullous impetigo and Staphylococcal Scalded Skin Syndrome (SSSS)?
explanation: In impetigo, the toxin acts locally at the site of infection, whereas in SSSS, the toxin spreads through the bloodstream to affect skin globally.
rationale: Think about how the toxin reaches different parts of the body in each condition.

optionExplanations.A: Both conditions are caused by $Staphylococcus$ $aureus$ and its specific exfoliative toxins.
optionExplanations.B: Both involve the superficial layers of the epidermis; the difference lies in the extent of the spread.
optionExplanations.C: In impetigo, the toxin acts locally at the site of infection, whereas in SSSS, the toxin spreads through the bloodstream to affect skin globally.
optionExplanations.D: Because both affect the very top layers of the skin, neither typically results in permanent scarring if treated correctly.
